subject: English
topic: Parallelism in lists and series of items
prompt: Fill in: She enjoys swimming, painting, and ___.
explain: Gerunds (swimming, painting) need a gerund: dancing.

subject: English
topic: Parallelism in lists and series of items
prompt: Choose the word that completes the series: The manager is honest, efficient, and ___.
explain: Honest, efficient are adjectives, so the third item must be an adjective: courageous.

subject: English
topic: Parallelism in lists and series of items
prompt: Which part is not parallel? "The course teaches us to think, to question, and acting independently."
explain: Two infinitives need a third infinitive: "to act independently".

subject: English
topic: Parallelism in lists and series of items
prompt: Complete: To read, to write, and ___ are basic skills.
explain: The series uses infinitives, so the last item must be "to calculate".

subject: English
topic: Parallelism in lists and series of items
prompt: Fill in: The job requires skill, patience, and ___.
explain: Skill and patience are nouns, so the last item must be a noun: dedication.

subject: English
topic: Parallelism in lists and series of items
prompt: Complete: He opened the door, switched on the light, and ___.
explain: Verbs in a series must share one tense: opened, switched, sat.

subject: English
topic: Parallelism in lists and series of items
prompt: Choose the correctly parallel sentence.
options: I came, saw, and to conquer.
I came, saw, and was conquering.
explain: All three verbs are in the simple past tense.

subject: English
topic: Parallelism in lists and series of items
prompt: Spot the non-parallel item: "The new phone is fast, light, and costs little."
explain: Fast and light are adjectives; "costs little" breaks the pattern. Use "cheap".

subject: English
topic: Parallel verb forms: gerund vs infinitive
prompt: Choose the parallel form: "Writing is as important as ___ ."
explain: Compared items must match: gerund 'Writing' pairs with gerund 'reading'.

subject: English
topic: Parallel verb forms: gerund vs infinitive
prompt: Fill in: "He prefers walking to ___ ."
explain: 'Prefer … to' compares gerunds: walking to driving.

subject: English
topic: Parallel verb forms: gerund vs infinitive
prompt: Complete: "It is better to give than ___ ."
formula: better to X than to Y
explain: Infinitive 'to give' needs the infinitive 'to receive' after 'than'.

subject: English
topic: Parallel verb forms: gerund vs infinitive
prompt: Complete: "She wants not only to sing but also ___ ."
formula: not only … but also: same form
explain: Correlatives join equal forms: 'to sing' with 'to dance'.

subject: English
topic: Parallel verb forms: gerund vs infinitive
prompt: Fill in: "He left without eating or ___ ."
explain: A preposition ('without') takes a gerund, so 'eating or drinking'.

subject: English
topic: Parallel verb forms: gerund vs infinitive
prompt: Correct the faulty item: "Her hobbies are reading, painting, and to travel."
explain: The series is gerunds, so 'to travel' becomes 'travelling'.

subject: English
topic: Parallel verb forms: gerund vs infinitive
prompt: Spot the error: "Their job is to design, build, and testing bridges."
explain: The one 'to' covers the series: to design, build, and test.

subject: English
topic: Parallel verb forms: gerund vs infinitive
prompt: Choose the correct: "She likes to cook, to paint, and ___ ."
explain: The series uses infinitives, so the last item must be 'to garden'.

subject: English
prompt: Spot the error: "Neither the manager or the clerk was present at the meeting."
explain: Neither is always paired with nor, never with or.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the parallel sentence: She wants ___.
options: either to sing or to dance
either to sing or dance too
explain: Both parts after either/or must have the same form: to sing … to dance.

subject: English
prompt: Either the teachers or the principal ___ going to attend the function.
formula: verb agrees with the nearer subject
explain: With either/or the verb agrees with the nearer subject, principal (singular).

subject: English
prompt: Neither she nor I ___ going to the party tonight.
explain: The verb agrees with the nearer subject I, so am is used.

subject: English
prompt: He both wrote the script and ___ the film.
explain: Both verbs must be in the same form: wrote … directed.

subject: English
prompt: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot the files.
explain: A sentence beginning with 'Not only' takes inversion: 'was he'.

subject: English
prompt: Not only the teacher but also the students ___ absent yesterday.
formula: Verb agrees with the nearer subject
explain: The verb agrees with the subject nearer to it: 'students' is plural, so 'were'.

subject: English
prompt: Both the captain and the coach ___ upset about the result.
formula: both A and B + plural verb
explain: 'Both … and' makes a plural subject, so it takes 'are'.

subject: English
prompt: He is not only interested in music but also ___ painting.
formula: repeat the same preposition in both parts
explain: Parallelism requires the same preposition: interested in … in painting.

subject: English
prompt: He likes both swimming and ___.
explain: The gerund 'swimming' needs a gerund after 'and': running.

subject: English
prompt: He was punished not only because he lied but also ___ he cheated in the test.
explain: Clauses after 'not only' and 'but also' must match, so 'because' is repeated.

subject: English
prompt: Pick the correct completion: He was both a gifted poet ___ a skilled painter.
explain: 'Both' pairs only with 'and'; 'but also' goes with 'not only'.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the parallel form: "She enjoys singing, dancing, and ___."
explain: Items in a series joined by 'and' must match: gerund, gerund, gerund.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in: "The post demands patience, accuracy, and ___."
explain: The series has nouns (patience, accuracy), so the last item must also be a noun: care.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in: "The plan was simple yet ___."
explain: 'Yet' joins two adjectives of equal rank: simple yet effective.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in: "He opened the door, looked inside, and ___ away."
explain: Verbs joined by 'and' stay in the same tense: opened, looked, walked.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in: "Would you rather walk to school or ___ the bus?"
explain: After 'rather', 'or' joins bare infinitives: walk or take.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in: "She is poor but ___."
explain: 'But' links an adjective to an adjective: poor but honest.

subject: English
prompt: Correct the faulty parallelism: "She likes to swim and cooking."
explain: An infinitive must pair with an infinitive: to swim and (to) cook.

subject: English
prompt: Seeing is more convincing than ___.
explain: Both items compared must be gerunds: seeing … than hearing.

subject: English
prompt: The climate of Shimla is cooler than ___ Delhi.
explain: Compare climate with climate; singular noun is replaced by 'that of'.

subject: English
prompt: Pick the correct completion: He is ___ Ravi.
options: as strong if not stronger as,
as strong as, if not stronger than,
as strong, if not stronger than,
explain: The first 'as' needs its own 'as': as strong as, if not stronger than.

subject: English
prompt: It is easier to promise than ___.
explain: Infinitive 'to promise' must be matched by infinitive 'to keep'.

subject: English
prompt: He is not so much a poet as ___.
explain: 'Not so much A as B' needs parallel forms: noun 'a poet' with noun 'a critic'.

subject: English
prompt: She would rather dance than ___.
explain: 'Would rather … than' takes the bare infinitive on both sides.

subject: English
topic: Comparing like with like (that of/those of)
prompt: Choose the correct form: 'Her voice is sweeter than ___.'
explain: A possessive ('her sister's') compares voice with voice; plain 'her sister' compares voice with a person.

subject: English
topic: Consistency of tense in parallel clauses
prompt: Choose the parallel verb: 'He entered the hall, looked around and ___ the lights.'
explain: Verbs in a narrative sequence joined by 'and' share the same tense: entered, looked, switched.

subject: English
topic: Consistency of tense in parallel clauses
prompt: Fill in: 'The teacher explained that water boils at 100°C and that ice ___ at 0°C.'
explain: Universal truths stay in the simple present, parallel with 'boils', even after a past reporting verb.

subject: English
topic: Consistency of tense in parallel clauses
prompt: Which verb breaks tense parallelism: 'He studies hard, wrote notes and revises daily'?
explain: The habitual present 'studies … revises' needs 'writes', not past 'wrote'.

subject: English
topic: Consistency of tense in parallel clauses
prompt: Fill in: 'If you work hard and ___ regularly, you will succeed.'
explain: Both verbs in the if-clause take the simple present; 'will' is not used in the if-clause.

subject: English
topic: Consistency of tense in parallel clauses
prompt: Fill in: 'She not only wrote the essay but also ___ it aloud to the class.'
formula: not only + V₁ … but also + V₁ (same tense)
explain: Correlative pairs need the same tense: 'wrote' is past, so the second verb is past 'read'.

subject: English
topic: Consistency of tense in parallel clauses
prompt: Spot the faulty part: 'Our teacher told us that the sun rises in the east and set in the west.'
explain: A universal truth takes the present tense, so 'set' should be 'sets', parallel with 'rises'.

subject: English
prompt: Which phrase keeps 'who' clauses parallel?
options: a boy who is talented and who is polite
a boy of talent and who is polite
a boy talented and who is polite
a boy who talented and is polite
explain: A relative clause must be matched by another relative clause with the same 'who'.

subject: English
prompt: Complete in parallel: My aim is to study law and ___ a judge.
explain: Infinitive phrase 'to study' needs a matching infinitive 'to become', not a gerund.

subject: English
prompt: Complete in parallel: She is not only intelligent but also ___.
explain: 'Not only … but also' joins like elements: adjective + adjective.

subject: English
prompt: Which series is correctly parallel in its use of prepositions?
options: by land, sea, and through by air
by land, by sea and air
by land, by sea and by air
by land, sea and by air
explain: Repeat the preposition for every item in the series, or omit it for all. Mixing the two breaks parallelism.

subject: English
prompt: Which phrase clearly refers to two different persons?
explain: Repeating the article before each noun marks separate persons; one article for both nouns suggests one person.

subject: English
prompt: Which part breaks parallelism: "The soup was hot, tasty and a delight."?
explain: Hot and tasty are adjectives. 'A delight' is a noun phrase, so it should be 'delicious'.

subject: English
prompt: Pick the parallel ending: 'The clerk typed the letter and ___.'
options: it was mailed to the client
to the client it got mailed
explain: 'Typed' is active, so the second verb 'mailed' must also be active in the compound predicate.

subject: English
prompt: Pick the parallel ending: 'The bridge was designed by Ravi and ___.'
explain: The passive 'was designed' pairs with the passive 'built by his team'. Active forms shift the voice.

subject: English
prompt: Pick the parallel ending: 'She likes to teach her pupils and ___ by them.'
explain: 'to teach' is active and 'to be respected by them' is passive. The infinitive form matches, and the 'by' phrase needs a passive.

subject: English
topic: Rather than / instead of parallel forms
prompt: Choose the correct form: "Instead of ___ for the test, he played video games all night."
explain: 'Instead of' is a preposition, so it takes a gerund (V-ing).

subject: English
topic: Rather than / instead of parallel forms
prompt: Choose the parallel form: "She decided to email the client rather than ___."
explain: After 'rather than', the verb matches the earlier 'to email', so it takes the base form: 'call'.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the parallel form: She enjoys ___.
options: to swim, cycling and to run
explain: Items in a series must share one form: all gerunds (swimming, cycling, running).

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: Living in a city is costlier than ___ in a village.
explain: Compared items must be parallel: gerund 'living' is compared with gerund 'living'.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: To err is human; ___ is divine.
explain: Infinitive 'to err' must be matched by infinitive 'to forgive'.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: His strengths are honesty, diligence and ___.
explain: Honesty and diligence are abstract nouns, so the third item must be a noun: punctuality.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: He opened the door, looked around and ___.
explain: Verbs in a series must share tense: opened, looked, walked.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: The clerk checked the files and ___.
options: the report was signed by him
explain: Keep the same subject and voice: 'checked… and signed…' are both active verbs.

subject: English
prompt: Spot the faulty parallelism: "The manager was efficient, courteous and had a lot of patience." Best correction:
explain: The series needs three adjectives: efficient, courteous, patient.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in: "Either you ___ or I have to go there."
explain: Verb agrees with the nearer subject (I) → have; 'you' also takes have.

subject: English
prompt: I do not like spicy food. Neither ___ my sister.
explain: Sentence-initial Neither forces inversion: Neither + auxiliary + subject. The auxiliary does matches the present tense.

subject: English
prompt: Complete in parallel: He explained why he was late and ___.
options: how he would make up for it
explain: A wh-clause ('why he was late') must be matched by another wh-clause: 'how he would make up for it'.

subject: English
prompt: Pick the parallel phrase: "The new model is faster, cheaper and ____ than the old one."
explain: Faster and cheaper are comparatives, so the third must be a comparative: more reliable.

subject: English
prompt: Pick the parallel phrase: "The film was either too long or ____."
explain: Either/or joins matching structures: 'too long' pairs with 'too slow'.

subject: English
prompt: Complete in parallel: He asked whether I was ready and ___ I had the tickets.
explain: The introducer 'whether' is repeated so both noun clauses stay parallel; 'that' cannot replace it.

subject: English
prompt: Complete in parallel: It is a book that informs and ___.
explain: One 'that' governs both verbs, so both must be in the same form: informs and entertains.

subject: English
prompt: Pick the parallel word: "Reading, writing and ____ are basic skills."
explain: Reading and writing are gerund nouns, so the third item must also be a gerund: counting.

subject: English
prompt: Pick the parallel word: "The plan is practical as well as ____."
explain: 'Practical' is an adjective, so the item joined by 'as well as' must be an adjective: economical.

subject: English
prompt: Pick the parallel word: "He behaved both foolishly and ____."
explain: Both…and joins like forms; 'foolishly' is an adverb, so use the adverb 'recklessly'.

subject: English
prompt: Pick the parallel word: "The difference between theory and ____ is vast."
explain: 'Theory' is a noun, so the word joined by 'and' must be a noun: practice.

subject: English
topic: Comparing like with like (that of/those of)
prompt: Spot the error: 'The eyes of an owl are larger than that of a cat.'
explain: 'Eyes' is plural, so the pronoun must be 'those of a cat'.
